title: The trace-formula local Frobenius agrees with the geometric-point local Frobenius
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, and the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: a finite extension $E/\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $K=(M,\theta)$ be an $E$-Weil complex [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], with $\theta:Lg_\gamma^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the geometric-Frobenius automorphism $g_\gamma=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$. Let $K_{\mathcal O}$ be a lattice of $M$ whose reductions $K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] for all $n\geq1$, as in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model], and take $\varphi_E=\theta$ there.

Let $x\in|X_0|$ be a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] and degree $e=[\kappa(x):k_0]$. Choose a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow k$; let $\bar x:s\to X$ be the associated geometric point and $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^e})$ the rational point it represents. Write $F^{\mathrm{trf}}_x=F_{y,e}$ for the $E$-stage local operator of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] on the stalk complex $K_{E,\bar x}=K_{\mathcal O,\bar x}\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$. Write $F_x$ for the local operator of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] on $C_{\bar x}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*M)$, formed with the same $\bar x$.

Then for every $j\in\mathbf Z$ there is an $E$-linear isomorphism
$$\mathrm H^j(K_{E,\bar x})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm H^j(C_{\bar x})$$
carrying $\mathrm H^j(F^{\mathrm{trf}}_x)$ to $F_x$. In particular, for every $j$,
$$\det\bigl(1-T^eF^{\mathrm{trf}}_x\mid\mathrm H^j(K_{E,\bar x})\bigr)=\det\bigl(1-T^eF_x\mid\mathrm H^j(C_{\bar x})\bigr)\quad\text{in }E[T],$$
and the same identities hold after scalar extension along $E\subset\Qlb$.

proof.text: Unpack the rationalization and point-fiber conventions. The proposition [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] identifies K_E with the rationalized object represented by K_O, while [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] defines Fib_s at E as Gamma(s,-) tensor_O_E E. Applying the rational derived pullback and then this point fiber to the same geometric point xbar therefore gives a canonical E-linear identification alpha: K_{E,xbar}=K_{O,xbar} tensor_O_E E -> C_{xbar}=Fib_s(L xbar^* M). It is natural in morphisms and hence will transport the induced endomorphisms and their cohomology maps.

proof.text: Fix the comparison families before comparing operators. Apply [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] with coefficient extension E=E to all compositions of xbar, g_X and g_s: use its c=eta^{-1} composed with R lim(c_n), formed on simultaneous strict reduction systems, and then rationalize. Its associativity, unit and scheme-morphism-equality clauses cover every iterate. These specify the integral composition isomorphisms whose rationalizations occur in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. This is a choice of the canonical construction supplied by the cited lemma, not an extra property of K or theta. In particular write G=Lg_X^*, J=Fib_s L xbar^* and c_e:L(g_X^e)^* -> G^e for these iterated comparisons. The same choice is used throughout the next step.

proof.text: The closed-point clause of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] gives e>=1, so apply [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] with m=e, y from the chosen residue embedding, and Lambda=E, using exactly the comparison families fixed in Step 2. Write t=t_{y,e,M}:JM -> JG^e M for its successive point transports and b_e=J(c_e^{-1}) composed with t. The normalization equation t=J(kappa^[e]) composed with rho, interpreted through c_e, identifies b_e with the rationalized scheme-Frobenius stalk transport tau_{y,e} in [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]. This uses the lemma's equality of specified strict-system maps and its integral realization and rationalization, not equality of unrelated maps inferred from their individual reductions. Here the return is g_X^e xbar=xbar g_s^e. The model proposition gives F^{trf}_x=phi_E^[e]_{xbar} composed with tau_{y,e}. Since phi_E=theta and all iterates use the same compositors, this iterated map is J(theta^[e]). The displayed local-Frobenius definition gives F^{geom}=J(theta^[e]) composed with b_e on C_{xbar}. Naturality of alpha from Step 1 therefore gives the typed equation alpha composed with F^{trf}_x = F^{geom} composed with alpha. Thus the comparison is already an intertwining isomorphism of point complexes.

proof.text: Apply the functor H^j to alpha and to the intertwining equality in Step 3. By [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules], H^j is functorial on the derived point-fiber categories, so H^j(alpha) is an E-linear isomorphism and carries H^j(F^{trf}_x) to F_x. The interpretation of the cohomology-sheaf stalk in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] identifies the target with the stated H^j(C_{xbar}), including degrees in which the complex is zero.

proof.text: Choose an E-basis of each finite-dimensional cohomology space and use H^j(alpha) to transport it. The two intertwined operators then have the same matrix, so multiplying by T^e and taking the finite determinant gives the displayed equality in E[T]. After extending scalars E to Qlb, the same matrix is carried coefficientwise to Qlb; the determinant polynomial is preserved by the ring homomorphism. This also covers the zero cohomology space, whose determinant is 1.
